Note: wrote the domain wall transform properly instead of the hack from friday. x = Ad + b, and a decoder that reads where the wall sits. round trip test on 5x3 passes. 1740 variables instead of 1914.
benchmark harness. four arms, seed loop, csv out. then realised I was giving dSB 1500 steps and SA 200 sweeps with no idea which is more work. the comparison means nothing as it stands.
timed one dSB step against one SA sweep. nowhere near equal. decided to fix wall clock instead of iteration count, 2.5s per run, and wrote a calibrator that scales the steps to hit it.

calibrator was off. asked for 1000 steps and got 686 because the setup cost is fixed and I was extrapolating from two points. made it iterate until it lands within 5%. now 2.41 to 2.56s across all four arms.
first honest 2x2. one-hot dSB is a disaster, 129 of 174 parcels invalid. domain wall fixes it. but domain wall also makes SA worse, which I was not expecting at all.

spent the morning trying to make the SA drop go away. it doesn't. 20 seeds each, it's real. the ordering penalty is set to 1.0 because I picked 1.0, and SA flips one bit at a time so the chain fights every move. dSB moves everything at once so it doesn't care.
stats. I was using wilcoxon signed rank. the seeds are independent runs, nothing is paired, so it should be mann whitney. redid every p value. conclusions didn't change but the test was wrong.
greedy baseline. best margin crop per parcel, then fallow parcels until the water fits. loses 1.58M. that is the entire argument of the paper sitting in one number.

checked whether greedy only loses because the demand curve goes negative past 2D. added free disposal, throw the surplus away instead of selling it. still loses 1.55M. so it's the glut, not the curve.
water sweep, lambda 0 to 4. on A/B demand peaks at 5.50 Mm3 and never reaches the 6.0 budget. shadow price is zero. I had assumed water was the binding constraint here and it isn't.
same sweep with Area C added. now it binds, 1.09 $/m3. so water only becomes scarce once the land opens up. that reframes the whole section.
Area C profit counterfactual. got 5.89M for full access against 5.36M restricted. felt too clean. left it and went to bed.

it was too clean. demand was being computed from whatever land regime I passed in, so the market grew at exactly the same rate as the supply and the loss just tracked land share. the ratio was 1.482, which is the area ratio to three decimals. that's what gave it away. pinned demand to A/B.

second problem with the same number. the 5.89M plan was using 8.17 Mm3 against a 6.0 budget, so I was comparing an infeasible plan against a feasible one. now reporting it as a range, 0.23M with the market fixed and 1.22M if the market scales with the land. wider but at least it's true.

pulled the soilgrids values for Area C and A/B side by side. pH 7.69 vs 7.71, clay 46.2 vs 46.4, CEC 34.2 vs 36.0, and organic carbon is actually higher in C. so there is no argument that the withheld land is poorer.
price robustness. shifted everything 15 and 30 percent both ways, plus perishables only, plus the LSTM vector.

the agreement metric is useless. two runs that differ only in the random seed agree on 12% of parcels. the optimum is degenerate, inverse demand equalises marginal revenue so hundreds of plans tie on profit. comparing parcel by parcel measures nothing.
switched to crop mix by area, 1 minus total variation distance. added a seed control run so there is a noise floor to compare against instead of comparing to 100%. floor comes out at 93%.
reran robustness with the mix metric. everything moderate sits within 2.4 points of the floor. only a 30% fall actually moves the plan, land shifts to grapes olives wheat and fallow.

figures. box plots not bar charts, the benchmarking papers are blunt about bars hiding the distribution and symmetric error bars lying about skew. three figures at column width, fonts set at final size so nothing gets rescaled.
paper skeleton in IEEEtran. abstract, intro, methods outline. six pages including references is going to be very tight.

LSTM evaluation. found a bug in the split, I was locating the target index with list.index which looks up by value, so any duplicate price sent the wrong window into test. positional now. result holds, LSTM still last.

ran the evaluation both ways. excluding 2024 persistence wins 130 against 252. including 2024 it flips. the war shock multiplies persistence error 4.9x and LSTM error only 2.5x, so a window with 2024 in it rewards robustness to a jump, not forecasting. excluding it.
the saved price forecast was contaminated, it was carrying 2024 forward as the 2025 estimate. oranges at 3611 $/t. rewrote the forecast capped at 2023 and regenerated.

actually read my own parameter table for once. wheat yield 0.59 t/ha. that is not a yield, PCBS says 2.7 rainfed. 586 is the wheat PRICE. the loader never found the yields file and fell back to sorted()[0] of the folder, which is the price file. silently. every number in the paper is wrong.

copied the real FAOSTAT yields file in. made the loader raise instead of guessing when it can't find exactly one match, and assert the units are actually kg/ha. real yields, wheat 2.41, grapes 9.38, oranges 19.38. everything downstream has to be rerun.

second bug and this one is worse. build(M=0) was zeroing both penalties, not just the one-hot one, so the domain wall arms were running with no suitability constraint at all. they were solving an easier problem and I was reporting it as an encoding win. split it into a separate M_onehot so the suitability penalty stays.

full rerun on correct data. benchmark, water sweep, area c, market scaling, robustness, figures. one-hot SA 5.42M, one-hot dSB 1.98M, domain wall dSB 5.00M. encoding gain 152%, SA penalty 8.5%, p 0.93 between the solvers under domain wall. all three findings survived the fix, which I was not confident about going in.
